Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

as soon as conjunction

also the moment, no sooner … than, once, the minute, the minute I saw you, as soon as possible

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.51 (Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 48.2: simul herbae incēperint nāscī, eximitō

simul atque (simul ac, simul)

conjunction, with the perfect indicative; the future perfect for the future

Simul alone is frequent (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ubi prīmum (ut prīmum, cum prīmum) — as soon as, the first moment

    conjunction, with the perfect indicative · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 104.6: ut prīmum gravitātem urbis excessī; Caes. B.G. 4.12: hostēs, ubi prīmum nostrōs equitēs cōnspexērunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 273; Traupman 382

    Quam prīmum is different: “as soon as possible”.

Examples

  • crēbrō runcātō. simul herbae incēperint nāscī, eximitō

    weed often; as soon as weeds begin to grow, pull them outCato Agr. 48.2

  • hāc rē vidēre nostra mala nōn possumus; aliī simul dēlinquunt, cēnsōrēs sumus

    that is why we cannot see our own faults; as soon as others go wrong, we are their judgesPhaedr. 4.10.4–5

  • ut prīmum gravitātem urbis excessī et illum odōrem culīnārum fūmantium … prōtinus mūtātam valētūdinem sēnsī

    as soon as I had left the heavy air of the city and that smell of smoking kitchens, I felt my health change at onceSen. Ep. 104.6

  • dictum ac factum

    no sooner said than doneTer. And. 381

  • extemplō ubi ego tē vīdī

    the minute I saw youTraupman 87

  • quam prīmum

    as soon as possibleTraupman 382

See also when, after.
